brief: Commitment of Traders data shows Non-Dealer S&P 500 futures selling continuing through September 29, led by Asset Manager accounts, which sold $11.7bn in the latest week against Non-Dealers' $10.5bn weekly total, extending a 5th week of selling in 6 since August 18 for a net -$63.7bn. Higher US 10-year real yields (up 25bp) and quarter-end rebalancing drove the selling: the rolling correlation between Asset Manager gross longs and real yields turned sharply negative, and reallocation may have started early. Subsequently, below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a weak payrolls report cut October hike odds, lifting the S&P 0.70%. But the December Adjusted Interest Rate future, a funding proxy, cheapened about 5bp, so deferred real rates rose and futures flow arguably stayed bearish. With Asset Manager net length still at a 77% 2-year rank before further likely sales, Goldman expects selling pressure to persist until yields reverse convincingly. GS rates research sees a clearer skew to lower yields ahead, despite upward pressure from oil and resilient AI investment plans.
